- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by +1–2% to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak.
- Model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from positive to negative, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 7-day average is >10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 2–4%.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.0s), model overestimates; apply downward correction of 1–3% to 3–5 day horizon.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00), model often drifts toward historical mean; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average of past 30 days.
